business_summary.text: Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals Limited is one of India's leading fertiliser companies, the largest private-sector manufacturer of Urea, and expanding into industrial and mining chemicals.

call_points.text: Fourth urea plant of about ₹10,000 Cr is under preparation; Board approval and financial bids are pending.
New urea policy is return-dilutive versus NIP-2012; scale benefits do not fully bridge the gap.
TAN project: weak nitric acid and ammonium nitrate solution production started; HDAN nearing commissioning.
IMACID is expanding phosphoric acid capacity from 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes, operational by April-June 2027.
Kharif sowing was 23% lower YoY at 183 lakh hectares by end-June, but July rains accelerated sowing.
Urea margin gains came from Gadepan-3 volumes, a currency uptick and surplus ammonia sales.
Complex fertiliser margins benefited from advance Kharif purchases and are expected to decline as prices average out.
Dividend policy of about 25% payout to be maintained; no buyback on the horizon.
NPK subsidy revision is delayed; industry seeks interim relief, government may act by October.
TAN market may be oversupplied for up to a year as domestic capacity rises; Reliance entry is a watch item.
Technical ammonium nitrate (TAN) project has entered the commissioning phase with dry runs underway for the weak nitric acid plant.

penalties.impact: No impact on financial, operation or other activities of the Company, save and except to the extent of amount of fine levied as above. The Company filed a waiver application dated May 20, 2026 outlining the reasons for the minor delay (few hours) in filing of SHP on NSE portal only i.e. the Company was under a bona-fide understanding/belief that the quarterly filing of SHP forms part of the unified submission mechanism, whereby submission on one stock exchange would be disseminated to the other exchange. NSE vide its letter dated July 8, 2026 has informed that the Company’s request for waiver of fine has been considered favourably.

guidance.statement: Fourth urea plant of about ₹10,000 Cr under preparation; Board approval pending, financial bids expected mid-October.
New urea plant expected to be delivered within 2030.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25%.

operating_notes.text: FY26 purchases of stock-in-trade rose 127.2% to ₹7,784.85 Cr, driving revenue growth alongside complex fertiliser sales.
Trade receivables rose to ₹2,075.20 Cr at Mar-2026 from ₹367.92 Cr a year earlier, and borrowings to ₹1,054.41 Cr from nil.
Technical Ammonium Nitrate project total cost is ₹1,645 Cr with a capacity of 2.4 Lakh MTPA.
TAN project capacity is 240,000 MTPA with target utilization of 75%-80% in its first year.
Weak nitric acid production commenced at the Gadepan site for the Technical Ammonium Nitrate project.
Q1 gas price was USD 17.25 per MMBtu on an NCV basis (provisional).
Subsidy received in Q1FY27 was ₹2,480 Cr versus ₹2,512 Cr last year; receivables at June 30 were ₹3,300 Cr, including ₹2,460 Cr subsidy.
IMACID phosphoric acid capacity is expanding from 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes, operational by April-June 2027.
Acquired 26% stake in Clean Max Hachi Private Limited for up to ₹6 crore to operate a 5 MW hybrid power plant in Rajasthan.

timeline.summary: Adventz Finance Private Limited, acting with Vishal Garodia and Mishd Grarodia, disclosed no new encumbrances on Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited shares under SEBI’s takeover rules as of April 2, 2026.
Shradha Agarwala, via V Venugopalan, disclosed no new encumbrances on Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals shares under SEBI’s takeover rules for FY2026.
Chambal Fertilisers commenced commissioning activities for its Technical Ammonium Nitrate project at Gadepan, targeting full production by May 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,785.03 Cr (+13.7% YoY), net profit ₹169.24 Cr.
On May 14, 2026, Chambal Fertilisers released its Q4FY26 and FY26 investor presentation showing consolidated revenue of ₹20,793.7 Cr and PAT of ₹1,953.3 Cr.

Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited shared the audio recording of its Analysts/Investors conference call on May 15, 2026, discussing FY-2025-26 financial results via investor.chambalfertilisers.com/files/CFCL_Q4_ConCall_Audio_FY-2025-26.mp3.
Hindustan Earthstone LLP, acting with concert parties, disclosed no new encumbrances on Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited shares for FY2026 under SEBI Regulation 31(4) on April 6, 2026.
On May 20, 2026, Chambal Fertilisers released the transcript of its Q4 FY26 earnings conference call held on May 15, 2026.
On June 1, 2026, Chambal Fertilisers announced the commencement of Weak Nitric Acid production at its Gadepan plant.
Krishna Shobhana Bhartia Family Trust declared no new encumbrances on Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2026.
Birla Real Estate Limited, acting with concert parties, disclosed no new encumbrances on Chambal Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2026.
Chambal's Q1FY27 call (July 31, 2026) flagged a ~₹10,000 Cr fourth urea plant pending Board approval, TAN commissioning progress and a 12% revenue decline offset by 12% EBITDA growth.
Chambal Fertilizers signed an agreement to acquire a 26% stake in Clean Max Hachi for up to ₹6 crore to develop a 5 MW hybrid captive power plant in Rajasthan.
